## Natural history notes

A small brown moth characterized by dark brown to chestnut-colored wings marked with scattered black dots and subtle wavy lines that help it blend into bark, leaf litter, and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, forests, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats with suitable vegetation and resting cover. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody or herbaceous plants and contribute to the broader food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
